newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-Siemens to invest in new UK unit.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Siemens to invest in new UK unit.

text.p: German engineering group Siemens plans to invest several million pounds over the next three to five years in Parsons Power Generation Systems, its new acquisition from Rolls Royce Plc
Rolls announced earlier it had agreed to sell the company to Siemens for 30 million stg.

Bob Hepburn, managing director of Siemens Power Generation told Reuters: "We will spend some money on improving the reliability and efficiency of the machine tools," at the Newcastle based plant in northern England.
"It will be several million pounds over the next three to five years," he said.
Hepburn saw no job losses among the 880 staff Siemens has agreed to take on. He said the future of the remaining 420 staff at the former Rolls Royce company would be decided by the British company.
Siemens first made an offer for the company in late January, he said, after Rolls put the division up for sale on July 19.

Hepburn said the group had gone through due diligence procedures and expected the deal to be approved by regulatory bodies within six to eight weeks. The acquisition will add 60 million of turnover to Siemens Power Generation's existing level of 250 million.
Siemens said it wanted to grow that figure but refused
to elaborate. Two thirds of the acquired business relates to provision of services to power stations in the UK and overseas.
The remainder will be obtaining manufacturing and engineering work for a factory in Germany.
He added there was scope for cost efficiencies and was confident of being able to provide employment for the 880 staff for "years to come".
